short: The final battle of the English Civil Wars, resulting in a total victory for Oliver Cromwell over Charles II and his Scottish army.
full:
On 3 September 1651, a massive Parliamentarian army commanded by Oliver Cromwell decisively defeated King Charles II at the Battle of Worcester. Charles had marched a Scottish army deep into England, hoping to spark a widespread Royalist uprising to reclaim his father's throne. However, very few English Royalists joined him, leaving his weary 16,000-strong army facing an overwhelmingly superior New Model Army of nearly 30,000 men.

The Parliamentarians assaulted the city from two sides, overwhelming the Scottish defenses in fierce, street-by-street fighting. Charles II barely escaped the city, embarking on a famous six-week flight across England in disguise before securing passage to France. The battle marked the definitive end of the English Civil Wars, destroying the last organized Royalist field army and cementing the authority of the Commonwealth across the British Isles.
